criteria.text: No change to the observable behavior of the purchase API or of PurchaseService; ADR 0011 and the security invariants continue to hold.
The existing purchase unit, integration, and system tests pass on the candidate.

findings.summary: The refactor drops the customer id from the idempotency submission fingerprint, so replaying a tenant-scoped Idempotency-Key against a different customer of the same tenant with the same timestamp and description returns the other customer's purchase (created=false) instead of 409 Conflict. This violates ADR 0011 ('same customer, timestamp, and normalized description') and returns a purchase of customer A on a request authorized only for customer B, with no resource access check on the returned purchase.
findings.evidence:
PurchaseService.java:168-171 (canonical = purchasedAt + "
" + description; base used customerId.value() + "
" + purchasedAt + "
" + description). Uniqueness is (tenant_id, idempotency_key): JdbcPurchaseRepository.java:41,51,54 and V9__create_purchase_history.sql:15. Probe runs/K1-pilot/probe/PurchaseCrossCustomerIdempotencyProbeTest.java fails on the candidate (C3: 'Expecting code to raise a throwable'; stdout 'replay on customer B returned purchase ... owned by customer A ..., created=false, sameAsA=true') and passes on base 88d7523 (C4).

findings.summary:
The fingerprint format change is incompatible with fingerprints already persisted in dokene.purchases.submission_fingerprint (database-immutable per ADR 0011): after deployment, a legitimate retry of a key recorded before deployment with an identical payload computes SHA-256(purchasedAt
description) and no longer equals the stored SHA-256(customerId
purchasedAt
description), so it gets 409 Conflict instead of the original purchase.
findings.evidence: PurchaseService.java:171 vs base PurchaseService.java fingerprint(); comparison at JdbcPurchaseRepository.java:54 (existing.fingerprint().equals(fingerprint)); immutability trigger V9__create_purchase_history.sql:62. Follows deterministically from the changed hash input; not exercised with a pre-deploy row.

checks.summary: Probe asserting ADR 0011 cross-customer key reuse yields PurchaseConflictException failed: replay on customer B returned customer A's purchase with created=false. Log runs/K1-pilot/candidate-tests.log.

checks.command: cd backend && ./gradlew test --tests '*PurchaseCrossCustomerIdempotencyProbeTest' (disposable worktree at base 88d7523, candidate patch reverted)
checks.summary: Control: the same probe passes on the base, so the behavior change is introduced by the candidate. Log runs/K1-pilot/base-probe.log.
checks.reusedBecause: Control run on the base content (tree of 88d7523, probe test added), not on the candidate; it supports F1 by contrast only and is not cited by any passing criterion.

limitations: F2 (incompatibility with fingerprints persisted before deployment) is established from code and the deterministic hash input change; it was not exercised against a pre-existing row.
Only purchase-scoped tests were run per benchmark memory limits; the full backend test suite and build were not run.
HTTP-level effect of F1 (controller returning another customer's purchase on POST) was not exercised; PurchaseController maps RecordResult directly, so the service-level probe covers it.
remainingActions: Restore customerId in the fingerprint canonical string (e.g. add it to the Submission record) so the hash input is byte-identical to the base: customerId + "\n" + purchasedAt + "\n" + description.
Add a regression test that reusing a key on another customer of the same tenant returns 409 Conflict, then re-verify.
